- **modify DR-38 (The skill ships inside the package, and setup installs…)**: one copy of the skill per repository (CLI-21).
  - decision, before: ~~The skill lives in the Python package, so installing the toolkit installs it. It is SKILL.md plus four reference pages: writing requirements, auditing, onboarding, and the rules page the checker links to. - `spec init` copies it to where each harness looks for skills: .claude/skills/syseng for Claude Code, and .agents/skills/syseng, the cross-tool location that Hermes and Antigravity read. Hermes loads a repository's skills only after `hermes skills trust`. - Each copy has the placeholder {{SPEC}} replaced by the toolkit's command, `spec`, and {{HARNESS_NOTES}} replaced by what that harness's hooks do, or by a note that none run. - The skill itself names no harness, tool or package manager. Harness-specific parts live in adapters.~~
  - decision, now:
    The skill lives in the Python package, so installing the toolkit installs it. It is SKILL.md plus four reference pages: writing requirements, auditing, onboarding, and the rules page the checker links to.
    - `spec init` writes one copy, in .agents/skills/syseng, the cross-tool location Hermes and Antigravity read. For Claude Code, which reads only .claude/skills, .claude/skills/syseng is a link to that copy. Hermes loads a repository's skills only after `hermes skills trust`.
    - The copy is the skill exactly as written: it has no placeholders and names no harness, tool or package manager.
    - What each harness's hooks do goes in the instruction-file section, which every harness reads.
  - consequences: ~~The installed copy is committed with the repository, so it can fall behind the toolkit. `spec init --check` reports the difference and `spec init` refreshes it. The rules page moved from docs/ into the skill.~~ → The installed copy is committed with the repository, so it can fall behind the toolkit; `spec init --check` reports the difference and `spec init` refreshes it. A checkout on a system without symlinks would see the link as a plain file, and Claude Code would miss the skill there. The rules page moved from docs/ into the skill.
